title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph I
statement: A graph has `n` nodes numbered `0` to `n - 1`, and node `i` carries the value `nums[i]`; the array `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Two distinct nodes `i` and `j` are joined by an undirected edge exactly when `|nums[i] - nums[j]| <= maxDiff`. Each `queries[k] = [u, v]` asks whether `v` can be reached from `u` by travelling along edges (a node always reaches itself). Return a boolean array whose `k`-th value answers `queries[k]`.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
signature: boolean[] pathExistenceQueries(int n, int[] nums, int maxDiff, int[][] queries)
notes:
## Intuition

Building the graph pair by pair and searching it per query costs O(n²) before any query is answered. Sorting changes everything: if `i < j` share an edge, every neighbouring gap between them is at most `nums[j] - nums[i] <= maxDiff`, so a walk through the indexes in between reaches `j` too. Components are therefore runs of consecutive indexes, and only the `n - 1` neighbouring gaps matter. A union-find joins each node to its left neighbour when that gap is small, and then a query is just two `find` calls.

## Approach

1. Give every node its own set: `parent[i] = i`.
2. `find(x)` climbs `parent` links to the root, halving the path as it goes.
3. For each `i` from 1, if `nums[i] - nums[i - 1] <= maxDiff`, hang the root of `i` under the root of `i - 1`.
4. For each query `[u, v]`, push whether `find(u)` and `find(v)` are the same root.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 2`, `nums = [1, 3]`, `maxDiff = 1`. `parent` starts as `[0, 1]`. At `i = 1` the gap is `3 - 1 = 2`, larger than 1, so nothing is joined. Query `[0, 0]`: both finds return `0`, so `true`. Query `[0, 1]`: the roots are `0` and `1`, so `false`. The answer is `[true, false]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + q): one join per gap and two finds per query, and since each new node is hung directly under its run's root, every `find` takes at most a step or two.
- Space: O(n) for `parent`, plus the answer array.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing only `nums[u]` and `nums[v]` misses paths through middle nodes: in Example 2, nodes 1 and 3 differ by 3 yet are connected through node 2.
- Do not build all O(n²) edges; neighbouring gaps already decide the components.
- A query with `u === v` is always `true`, and `u` may be larger than `v`; comparing roots handles both.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parent` | union-find links; a root points to itself |
| `find` | returns the root of a node's run |
| `i` | the node being joined to its left neighbour |
| `answer` | one boolean per query |
| `u`, `v` | the endpoints of the current query |

narration.2: Every node starts alone, as the root of its own set.
narration.4: find returns the root that represents a node's set.
narration.5: Keep climbing while x is not a root.
narration.6: Path halving: point x at its grandparent so later searches are shorter.
narration.9: x points to itself, so it is the root.
narration.12: Look at each neighbouring pair of the sorted values, left to right.
narration.13: A gap of at most maxDiff means an edge between i - 1 and i.
narration.14: Join the two runs by hanging i's root under the root of i - 1.
narration.19: Take the two endpoints of each query.
narration.20: A path exists exactly when both endpoints share a root.
narration.22: Return the answers in query order.
